steps.description: Attacker submits a malicious governance proposal (BIP-18) that, if executed, will transfer all treasury funds to the attacker's address. The proposal is disguised with an innocuous title. No bond or minimum token holding is required to submit proposals.

Attacker takes a massive flash loan from Aave — borrowing $3 billion in stablecoins across USDC, DAI, and USDT. The flash loan must be repaid within the same transaction, but gives the attacker temporary control of enormous capital.

Attacker deposits the flash-borrowed stablecoins into Beanstalk's Silo to receive Stalk (governance) tokens. The $3B deposit gives the attacker approximately 67% of total Stalk supply — well above the 50% quorum needed. The protocol allows immediate voting power upon deposit.

Attacker votes FOR their malicious proposal with 67% of the total Stalk. The Beanstalk governance allows emergencyCommit — if a proposal reaches quorum, it can be executed immediately without waiting for the timelock period. The attacker votes and executes in the same transaction.

The malicious proposal executes, transferring all $182M from the Beanstalk treasury to the attacker's contract. The DAO contract calls transfer on every token in the treasury, draining BEAN, USDC, ETH, and LP tokens. This is irreversible on-chain.

Attacker withdraws their deposited stablecoins from the Silo (burning the Stalk), repays the $3B flash loan plus the ~0.09% fee ($2.7M). Net profit: $182M stolen minus $2.7M in flash loan fees = ~$179.3M. The entire attack executes in a single atomic transaction.
